newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks forge ahead in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks forge ahead in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks marched ahead strongly in early Friday trade on robust buying demand, derived from expectations of flat interest rates and upward revisions in corporate earnings, brokers said.
"The market declines have been on lower volume than market gains, suggesting that upward momentum is still strong," said Adam Conn at HSBC James Capel.
The Hang Seng Index put on 57.41 points to 12,535 on robust turnover of HK$1.70 billion.
"A lot of investors expected earnings momentum to decline in 1997, but we are now looking at brighter prospects," Conn added.
The brokerage has revised upward its expectations for the residential property market and those related stocks and for retailers, Conn added.

Brokers said both overseas and the local investors' appetite for Hong Kong shares was whetted by U.S. Labour Department data pointing to flat job growth and indirectly suggesting flat or declining interest rates in the United States and Hong Kong.
Technical indicators are also giving a very bullish picture, said New Century Securities research manager Alan Shum, adding that on more fundamental grounds he was more cautious.
"The market's short-term consolidation is over but investors are still waiting for confirmation," said Shum.
"Technically speaking, if we see the index close above the 12,550-level today, the index will be on its way to forming a new uptrend."
The Hang Seng Index is already above its record closing level of 12,510.05 set on October 18 but somewhat below its record intraday high of 12,602.34 set on October 16.
The finance sector led the market from the opening, followed the property sector. H shares were also firmer on the back of improved earnings outlook.
HSBC Holdings soared to a new all time high of HK$159.50 then eased to trade up HK$0.50 at HK$159.50. Hang Seng Bank put on only HK$0.25 to HK$92.00.
In the property sector New World Development put on HK$1.00 to HK$46.00. The company announced on Friday that it would raise to US$350 million the sum of its convertible bond issue.
Henderson Land put on HK$0.75 to HK$69.50 and Henderson Investment was unchanged at HK$8.45. Among the H shares Shanghai Petrochemical gained HK$0.05 to HK$2.125.
